mandatoryFindings.title: Execution consumes unverified second dependency buffers
mandatoryFindings.facts: bootstrap hashes predicates.py in its three-file loop, then rereads predicates.py and compiles the new buffer without hashing it. helpers similarly hashes safe_bytes(CORE), then parses a second safe_bytes(CORE). Per-read custody cannot establish equality across these distinct stable reads.
mandatoryFindings.pairedEvidence: independent-check-results.json cases bootstrap/CORE same verified bytes, wrong first pin, changed second read. Bad first pins HOLD without execution. Correct first pins followed by changed second buffers execute marker-only synthetic code without HOLD in both sites.
mandatoryFindings.impact: The exact no-dependency-execution-before-pin requirement from FR-CODE-05/rootab992 remains unsatisfied. A later whole-file hash check cannot undo already executed unverified code. No actual tampering or runtime execution is alleged.
mandatoryFindings.requiredFix: Compile/parse the exact retained byte buffer whose digest was checked, or independently hash the actual execution buffer immediately before its use. Apply to both policy bootstrap and reused CORE extraction. Add adversarial changed-between-read pairs to the faithful actual-definition harness; reseal a new author packet.

mandatoryFindings.title: Policy bootstrap weakens custody member names before malformed-journal dereference
mandatoryFindings.facts: The adapter initially defines canonical as a single-component member check, but bootstrap replaces that global with predicates.canonical, which accepts nested relative names. Custody.read/write consult that mutable global. validate_negative reads denial.clientJournal before negative_record checks the complete schema and exact derived single-component name. Retained custody covers ancestors through HERE, not any extra components in a nested member name.
mandatoryFindings.pairedEvidence: supplemental-check-results.json: actual extracted Custody/local/validate_negative with a synthetic malformed journal name nested/proof.json and in-memory linked nested ancestor. The original component-only predicate rejects MEMBER_NAME before the nested body. The post-bootstrap predicate reads the synthetic nested body, then rejects NEGATIVE_SCHEMA.
mandatoryFindings.impact: Malformed data can reach an unqualified nested body before eventual HOLD. O_NOFOLLOW on the leaf alone does not protect additional intermediate member components. This is a read-boundary defect, not a demonstrated closing allow. An already-present extra directory would fail initial namespace validation; the reproduced edge is the continuing read boundary after bootstrap/initial membership inspection. No actual nested or private body was read.
mandatoryFindings.requiredFix: Keep a non-overwritable component-only validator for all Custody member names and reject malformed journal schemas/names before dereferencing them. If nested names are deliberately supported, retain and validate every extra ancestor descriptor instead. Add actual-function paired malformed-name tests and reseal a new author packet.
